round4.reason_for_inconclusive: the execution sandbox forbids ALL filesystem writes, including scratch. The checker did not attempt prohibited mutations and did not claim the maker's receipt as independent evidence. The INCONCLUSIVE is therefore a SANDBOX LIMITATION, not a product failure -- but the checker ALSO found three real product defects, which are real regardless of the sandbox.

product_defects_found.what: tests/test_reproducible_build.py:335 converted ANY failed build into a SkipTest, including product defects -- not merely a verified missing backend. A blanket skip on any nonzero exit lets a broken build hide behind an unavailable backend.
product_defects_found.fixed_in: the skip is now conditional on a missing-backend marker; any other build failure raises AssertionError, so a product defect FAILS instead of skipping

product_defects_found.what: the W1 regression test accepted either boolean result (`_has_build(...) in (True, False)`), so it asserted nothing: the checker verified the interpreter independently, but the assertion did not enforce rejection.
product_defects_found.fixed_in: the test now asserts the probe returns a real bool AND agrees with `python -m build --version`, and that a backend-less interpreter is rejected with a clean False

product_defects_found.what: the mutation probe treated ANY nonzero pytest exit as a caught mutation, so a collection or infrastructure error could masquerade as a meaningful kill.
product_defects_found.fixed_in: _pytest_counts() parses the summary line; a nonzero exit with zero collected tests, or with no failed/errored test, is now a probe FAILURE, not a claimed kill

swarm_audit_findings.what: the probe's git environment was inherited wholesale with only GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_INDEX_FILE overridden; GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY and other relocation variables could still point into the protected repository
swarm_audit_findings.fixed_in: _isolated_git_env() strips every git-location variable from the inherited environment and gives the copy a private GIT_COMMON_DIR

swarm_audit_findings.what: copytree(symlinks=True) preserved symlinks, so a mutation writing to a linked file could follow it back into the protected tree -- the isolation was complete only at the git layer
swarm_audit_findings.fixed_in: symlinks=False, so a link is copied as a regular file and a mutation cannot traverse it

round4.swarm_audit_false_positive: the auditor reported that two files in the protected tree changed during the probe run. Verified independently: those are the orchestrator's OWN concurrent edits to the two test files; the protected repository's staged tree, HEAD and cached diff were unchanged throughout. The write-through did NOT occur, and the git-level isolation holds.
round4.claim_ceiling: this is a real, complete, independently-produced verdict, and it says INCONCLUSIVE / NOT ACCEPTED. It is NOT an acceptance. The three product defects it found were fixed in this round and re-measured on the maker side; a further independent round is required before the candidate can be accepted.
